code_first.q: Use a different class dataset to filter marks, then connect the result to SQL.
code_first.code:
array names = ["Eli","Jo","Sam"]
array marks = [65,52,38]
for i = 0 to 2
    if marks[i] >= 60 then
        print(names[i])
    endif
next i
p: Predict which name prints when the threshold is 60.
Change the threshold to 50 and predict which names print.
Add a counter for qualifying pupils; explain why only necessary personal fields should be selected.
code_first.a: At threshold 60, code prints Eli. At 50 it prints Eli then Jo. A counter initialised to 0 before the loop and incremented inside the IF gives 1 and 2 respectively. SQL can express the same filtering, e.g. SELECT Name FROM Scores WHERE Mark >= 60; data minimisation means processing only necessary personal data.

original_exam_questions: Write SQL to display Name from Pupils for pupils whose Mark >= 70. [3 marks]
SELECT Name [1] FROM Pupils [1] WHERE Mark >= 70 [1]; Ada and Mia match.
Complete a code condition so that names[i] is printed only when marks[i] < 50. State the result using the shared data. [3 marks]
IF marks[i] < 50 THEN [2 for correct condition/control] print(names[i]) [1]; prints Ben.
Explain why comparing '72' directly with numeric 50 can be problematic when reading marks from a CSV text file. [3 marks]
readLine() supplies text [1]; '72' is a string, while 50 is numeric [1]; the field must be converted/validated before a numerical comparison [1].

optional_original_challenge.coreHint: This Code First dataset is different from the modelled Pupils table. Read the three marks before setting the threshold.

stretch.task: For the separate Scores table (Eli=65, Jo=52, Sam=38), change code and SQL to select names with Mark < 60.
stretch.hint: Update condition to marks[i] < 60; query SELECT Name FROM Scores WHERE Mark < 60;
stretch.answer: Code prints Jo and Sam in that order. SQL returns those same names; SQL row order is not guaranteed without an ORDER BY.

mastery.task: Optional integration: read pupils.csv, skip the header, split each line, validate/cast Mark, build a table-like structure and return pupils with numeric Mark >= 50. Compare the result with SQL, and explain how erroneous data should be handled.
mastery.hint: Use file open/read/close, split on comma in the chosen high-level language, convert numeric fields safely, then loop/filter. Only attempt after the core loop is secure.
mastery.answer: Expected names Ada and Mia. Ben 43 is excluded. A correct outline opens file; discards ID,Name,Mark header; reads/splits each row; checks number fields; converts mark to integer; tests >=50; prints corresponding names; closes file; rejects or reports malformed/non-numeric data. The SQL result contains the same names, with no guaranteed order.
